The search returned many templates but not clearly the Heck coupling. The first result seems unrelated. We need a template that forms C-C bond between aryl bromide and alkene (Heck). The returned templates have reaction_id etc. We need template_id (maybe reaction_id?). The description says template_id is string. The returned dict includes 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash' etc. Probably template_id is the reaction_id as integer? In example they used numeric template_id. So we can use reaction_id.

We need a template that matches our reactants: 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (SMILES: Brc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1) and N-phenylacrylamide (SMILES: O=C(Nc1ccccc1)/C=C/). The product would be target minus HCl? Actually product: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. Wait we also need p-tolyl amine later.

Our first step: Heck coupling of 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride with N-phenylacrylamide to give intermediate B: S(=O)(=O)Cl attached to phenyl which now has side chain C=C-CO-NH-Ph. That intermediate B SMILES: ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2)cc1. (No tolyl yet). Then second step: sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine (SMILES: Cc1ccc(N)cc1). Reaction: p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride -> target, releasing HCl.

Thus we need two reaction templates: one for Heck coupling (aryl bromide + alkene -> aryl-alkene) and one for sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide). We need template IDs for these.

Search for sulfonamide formation template: functional groups formed maybe "sulfonamide". Use search with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamide"].
